title_candidates: ChatGPT for Teens adds study hours and stronger safeguards
summary: ChatGPT now gives 13-to-17-year-olds a learning-focused experience with stronger defaults, Study Hours, break reminders, and family controls.

primary_source.title: Introducing ChatGPT for Teens: Built for learning, backed by protections
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: Users identified as 13 to 17 are placed into the teen experience.
The experience includes Study Mode, homework reminders, quizzes, visual explanations, Study Hours, and break reminders.
Teen defaults add stronger protections around several high-risk and age-inappropriate subjects.
Linked guardians can manage selected settings but cannot read conversations or live activity.

supporting_sources.title: Managing parental controls in ChatGPT
key_facts: Either the teen or guardian can start account linking.
Study Hours changes how eligible chats begin; Quiet Hours blocks access during selected times.
Either person can unlink, and the guardian is notified when the teen unlinks.

supporting_sources.title: Using study mode in ChatGPT
key_facts: Study Mode is available across ChatGPT plans on web, iOS, and Android.

prerequisites: Separate ChatGPT accounts for a teen and parent or guardian
Access to the invitation email or phone number

steps.instruction: Link the separate teen and guardian accounts through Settings > Parental controls.
Review safeguards, data, media, Study Mode, Study Hours, and Quiet Hours together.
Use Study Mode on a harmless known topic and check its explanation and practice questions.
Agree on school-policy, verification, privacy, and human-support boundaries.

references.title: Introducing ChatGPT for Teens: Built for learning, backed by protections
references.author: OpenAI

risk_flags: Safety controls can fail and do not replace trusted adults, professionals, or emergency services.
Parental controls do not expose teen conversations or live activity.
